title: Black beans with green chiles and cumin (instant pot)

ingredients.name: finely chopped fresh sage (or marjorem or oregano)
kosher salt, plus more as needed
bunch fresh cilantro, stems and leaves separated
small bunch scallions, white and green parts separated, thinly sliced
Grated Monterey Jack cheese, for serving (optional)

steps.text: Roast poblano and jalabenos over an open flame on stove, or under broiler, until their skins are blistered and charred all over, about 10 minutes. Transer to a bowl, cover with plate, and let them sit until they are cool enough to handle. Then rub the skins off with a paper towel, and seed and dice the chiles.

Using the saute function, heat 2 tbs of the oil in the pressure cooker. Stir in the onion and cook until golden, about 15 minutes. Stir in the sage, two-thirds of the minced garlic, and the chili powder and cumin; cook for 1 minute. Stir in the chopped poblanos, hal of the jalapenos and the beans, salt, and 5 cups of water. Cover and cook on high pressure for 40 minutes. Allow the pressure to release naturally. If the beans aren't cooked through, cook on high pressure for 5 minutes, then manually release pressure.

While beans are cooking, in a blender combine the tomato, cilantro stems, half the cilantro leaves, scallion whites, the remaining garlic, the remaining 3 tbs oil, the remaining jalapenos, and a large pinch of salt. Blend, then taste and add more salt and pepper if necessary.
When beans are cooked, stir in the tomato puree and let sit for 5 minutes. Then, if the mix seems thin, simmer using the saute function for a few minutes to thicken it up.
Transer beans to individual serving bowls and top with cheese, cilantro leaves, and thinly-sliced scallion greens. Serve with lime wedges.
